name: The Queen's Room
firstVisit: Dust, everywhere, lying flat and even. Nobody has walked in here for a very long time.
It's cold. Colder than the corridor. Colder than it has any right to be.

W: Pale stone, not black. This room was finished before the castle got its new colour scheme.
1: The corridor. It's warmer out there. Noticeably.
5: A portrait of the old queen, painted over, like the one in the hall.
Here someone has painted over the whole thing, frame and all, and then hung a small picture of a bowl of fruit in front of it.
It's a very nice bowl of fruit. Nobody has ever looked at it.
M: A tall mirror, gone grey with dust.
You don't wipe it. You couldn't say why. You just don't.
6: The open hand, holding a sword by the blade: the old crest.
Everywhere else in the castle it's been covered by a fist. In here, nobody bothered. Or nobody dared.
y: A vanity table, its drawers shut. A pot of rouge gone hard as a stone. A ribbon, faded to no colour at all.
Q: A great bed, made five hundred years ago and not slept in since. The dust has settled into the exact shape of the blankets.
It's a very good bed. Nobody wants it.
T: Roses in a vase, dried on the stem. Five hundred years, and they still haven't quite fallen apart.
They smell, very faintly, of roses. That's the worst part.
7: A writing desk. Ink dried to a crust in the well, and a quill put down in the middle of a sentence.
The sentence is gone. The quill is still waiting.
w: A wardrobe. Locked, with the key left in the lock. You leave it there.
h: A pale rug, patterned with roses. The only rug in the castle that wasn't brought back from a war.

objects.name: Maid Dorrit
lines: Oh! You can't— well. You can. Nobody says you can't. Nobody comes in, is all.
I dust the doorway. Just the doorway. Forty years, and I've never got further than this tile.

questions.ask: Why is it so cold in here?
answer: Always has been. Summer, winter. Light every fire in the castle and it'd still be cold in here.
The old housekeeper said it was the stone. The one before her said it was the queen.
The one before HER didn't say anything. She just stopped coming upstairs.
The old queen's. Before the king. The king before this king, I mean.
Beautiful, they say. Too beautiful, my nan said, but my nan said that about bread.
She went missing, and the old king went strange, and then there was a new king. That's all anybody knows. That's all anybody's allowed to know.

questions.ask: Do the king's queens ever come in?
answer: Never. Queen Brunhilt put her head round the door once, her first week.
She came straight back out and asked for a different room. Any room. She said the mirror looked at her funny.
She's got the second-worst room now, and she's never once complained. Well. Never about that.

questions.ask: Forty years dusting one doorway? Pathetic.
answer: You can see yourself in it. Not in the mirror. In the doorway. That's how clean.
Mind it on your way out. I've just done it.
